01

About Me

I am a doctoral researcher working at the intersection of trustworthy machine learning, natural language processing, and human-centred computing. My research explores how intelligent systems can remain reliable, understandable, and useful in high-impact settings.

I am currently advised by Professor R. Sharma and collaborate with the Responsible Computing Lab. Before beginning my doctorate, I worked on applied data-science projects in healthcare and education.

My goal is to build AI systems that people can understand, question, and confidently use.

02

Current Research

Reliable language models for public services

This project studies uncertainty estimation, factual consistency, and human oversight for language models used in information-access systems.

Methods: retrieval-augmented generation, calibration, evaluation design, and participatory user studies.

Explainable decision support

We are developing explanation methods that adapt to the needs of domain experts and affected users rather than providing a single technical explanation for everyone.

06

Featured Projects

Bharosa — Model reliability toolkit

An open-source toolkit for measuring calibration, subgroup performance, and failure patterns in classification and language-model pipelines.

Technologies: Python, PyTorch, FastAPI, and Docker
Source code · Project page

Samvaad — Multilingual research assistant

A research prototype for retrieving and summarizing public documents across Indian languages, with citations and human-verification controls.

Technologies: Python, vector search, JavaScript, and accessibility testing

Reproducible AI benchmark

A documented benchmark and dataset card for studying robustness under language and domain shift.
